item.title: The Joel Embiid and LeBron James adjustment that could make the 76ers more dangerous
item.description: Source: headlinephotos/Depositphotos A superstar arrives, the whole league watches, and everyone expects fireworks. Yet the smartest moments often come from small ideas that nobody planned. Philadelphia basketball fans just got a fresh example of that this fall. Joel Embiid and LeBron James now share a locker room, a pairing few fans ever saw coming. Expectations are huge, and every early game feels like a test of whether this bold experiment can work. A foul problem hits the 76ers Late in the second quarter, Joel Embiid picked up his third foul with the 76ers trailing 50-46. Coach Nick Nurse went small and brought in Anfernee Simons for some much-needed offensive spark. Foul trouble can wreck a night for a franchise center. Embiid wanted to stay on the floor and still defend hard. He needed a creative answer before the second half began, and halftime provided it. The matchup mattered because New York leaned on center Karl-Anthony Towns. He averaged 7.5 assists per game when the Knicks swept Philadelphia in the playoffs, acting as a trigger at the top of the offense. The halftime idea that changed everything At halftime, Embiid suggested that LeBron James take over the defensive assignment on Karl-Anthony Towns. Embiid would guard Josh Hart in a roaming role and provide help around the lane. The coaching staff agreed, and the plan went into motion. The logic was simple. A strong forward could hold his ground against a center, which meant Embiid no longer had to take as many risks. He could protect the rim while trying to avoid additional fouls and stay on the court. James accepted the assignment and took on the physical challenge. That willingness gave Nurse another defensive option he could use when the matchup demanded it. LeBron takes on Towns in the paint Towns is a skilled big man who punishes weak coverage. Slowing him takes patience, quick feet, and smart help from teammates. James has the size and experience to handle that type of assignment. James scored 14 points and handed out 7 of the 76ers’ 28 assists. Those numbers look modest by his standards, but his impact also came through defensive coverage and decisions that created opportunities for teammates. James accepted the difficult assignment of defending Towns in his Philadelphia regular-season debut. The adjustment helped the 76ers settle defensively after halftime. item.title: Dodgers owner Mark Walter breaks silence on idea of potentially selling team
item.description: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images Dodgers owner Mark Walter breaks silence on idea of potentially selling team appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Los Angeles Dodgers owner Mark Walter rejected the possibility of selling the franchise, addressing speculation about its future after unloading other sports investments. His comments followed months of questions surrounding his ownership and a federal investigation into businesses within his financial empire. Walter said his sale of his Los Angeles Lakers stake had nothing to do with the Dodgers, separating that transaction from his plans for the baseball team. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The remarks also came after Los Angeles’ season ended with a National League Championship Series sweep against the Milwaukee Brewers. In an interview with the California Post’s Jack Harris, Walter reaffirmed his intention to retain the club and continue pursuing championships. “We’re going to keep the team no matter what,” he said. “We’re going to be winning for 10 years or more. I think our commitment to do so will be just like it has been in the past. And, you know, we don’t win every year, but we’re going to try to.” Walter helped lead the Guggenheim Baseball Management group that bought the Dodgers for $2.15 billion in 2012. He owns roughly 27 percent of the franchise. Under that ownership, Los Angeles won World Series championships in 2020, 2024 and 2025. This year’s NLCS defeat ended its pursuit of a third consecutive title. The ownership questions intensified after the federal investigation became public in July. Walter subsequently sold his Lakers stake to Josh Kushner and Bob Iger at a $12.5 billion valuation. He also sold his Chelsea stake and reportedly has explored selling the WNBA’s Los Angeles Sparks. Dodgers president Stan Kasten twice denied a sale during the season. TWG Global likewise said the franchise was not for sale and that no sale process had begun. Walter declined to discuss the investigation into his insurance companies, Delaware Life and Clear Springs Life and Annuity. His comments leave the Dodgers preparing for another season under the same ownership. item.title: Jayson Tatum adds to clutch resume with latest Celtics game-winner
item.description: BOSTON — What makes an NBA player clutch comes down to how they perform in crunch time. However, whether or not somebody earns that "clutch" label is often decided by narratives, not facts. So, what do the statistics say about Boston Celtics star Jayson Tatum? Although the six-time All-Star has never won Clutch Player of the Year since it became an NBA award in 2022, the numbers suggest that Tatum is near the top of the league in terms of making big-time shots. Tuesday night provided the latest evidence of that, as Tatum drained a game-winning jumper at the buzzer in overtime to give the C's a 125-124 victory over the Brooklyn Nets . The data that followed this huge shot does a lot to bolster Tatum's clutch resume. For example, according to Max Lederman of NBC Sports Boston , Tatum is now tied for the most made field goals to tie or take the lead in the final 10 seconds of a game since the 2017-18 season. The 2024 NBA champion has delivered 17 of those buckets, tying Denver Nuggets guard (and future Hall of Famer) DeMar DeRozan. Need evidence that dates back even further? Since the 1996-97 campaign, no other player has a higher field goal percentage on shots to tie or take the lead in the last 24 seconds of a game (on at least 60 attempts), per Stathead . Tatum's conversion rate of 38.7 percent is just ahead of Dallas Mavericks legend Dirk Nowitzki. "JT had the ball in his hands and made the right play for himself and for others," Celtics head coach Joe Mazzulla said in the wake of the home win. "And there's no other guy I'd rather have it." The rest of Tatum's outing was impressive, too. The 28-year-old logged 40 points, 8 assists, and 0 turnovers against the Nets, becoming the second Celtic ever to record that statline and hit a game-winning buzzer-beater on the same night, per NBC Sports Boston statistician Dick Lipe . The legendary Larry Bird is the only other Celtic to ever accomplish such a feat. Paul George on Jayson Tatum’s game-winner: “Got the ball to the MVP, and he took us home.” pic.twitter.com/QcJ58AAxuo — Daniel Donabedian (@danield1214) October 28, 2026 "You're in a different zone," Celtics wing Paul George described when asked what it's like once a potential game-winner goes up. "It's literally quiet. And then once the shot goes in, it's that excitement when the crowd erupts. It brings out that fire in you." The 3-1 Celtics will need Tatum to keep that competitive fire burning on Friday night as they seek their fourth straight win when they host the Chicago Bulls as part of NBA Cup group play. item.title: City march on with dramatic penalty shootout win over Brighton
item.description: City march on with dramatic penalty shootout win over Brighton City battled back twice before beating Brighton in a rollercoaster penalty shootout to reach the fifth round of the Carabao Cup. After Mateo Kovačić and Vitor Reis equalised to see the game finish 2-2 after 90 minutes, Gerónimo Rulli saved Brighton’s last two penalties to see us into the next round. Malick Yalcouye put the visitors ahead in the first half before Kovačić levelled before the break, firing in a low shot from outside the box. Brighton grabbed a second shortly after the restart through Georginio Rutter and a record Etihad Stadium domestic cup crowd of 55,345 urged us forward to get a second equaliser. It came with just under 20 minutes remaining when Reis got his first City goal as he flicked in Rayan Cherki’s low free-kick before a dramatic 4-3 win on penalties with Rulli the hero. THE MATCH IN BRIEF City started with a young line-up that included four Academy players while midfielder Kovačić was six years older than any of his outfield team-mates. And the Croatian showed his all his craft with a well-taken strike to fire City level after we’d fallen behind to Yalcouye’s opener on the half-hour. Rayan Cherki, one of only two players with Marc Guéhi to keep their place from the weekend, had led the Blues charge early on. Firstly, earning a dangerous free-kick after leading a break from his own half before teeing up Phil Foden’s whose low cross deserved a touch. Brighton, who knocked out Manchester United in the previous round, had the first two efforts on target but they were easily collected by Gerónimo Rulli on his second City appearance. Pascal Gross drove another low shot just wide before Georginio Rutter fired in a low cross that was turned by Yalcouye, who appeared to be offside but was just the right side of City’s Ayyoub Bouaddi. But before they could get acclimatised to their new positions, Brighton were ahead when Georginio turned in Jaouen Hadjam’s low cross. The introduction of Jérémy Doku gave City some attacking pep and Rico Lewis and Cherki were both off-target as we chased a second equailser. item.title: Kompany discharged from hospital following collapse
item.description: Kompany was appointed Bayern Munich manager in May 2024 [Getty Images] Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany has been discharged from hospital and is "doing well" following his collapse at the club's training ground. Kompany, 40, was rushed to hospital last Friday after taking ill as he watched the club's second team train. The cause has been identified as meningeal irritation - an inflammation of the protective membrane surrounding the brain and spinal cord. "Given the circumstances, he's doing well," Max Eberl, the club's board member for sports, told German broadcaster ARD on Wednesday. "He was discharged from the hospital today. That is the biggest and best news for all of us." No timeline has been set for Kompany's return and Bayern said on Saturday that it would be a matter of "weeks, not days" until the former Manchester City defender returned to the dugout. English assistant coach Aaron Danks has taken over in Kompany's absence and oversaw a 3-1 win at Freiburg on Sunday. Kompany had been nursing a virus in the days before his collapse and missed some team training sessions. The Belgian missed a pre-match news conference prior to Bayern's Champions League game against Arsenal last Tuesday, but was subsequently on the touchline for the match on Wednesday. "It's a meningeal irritation that caused this incident on Friday. He will now rest and take medication," said Eberl, speaking before Bayern's German Cup tie against Magdeburg. "I am very confident that he will be back on the touchline, operating at 100% very soon." Current leaders Bayern face title rivals Borussia Dortmund in the Bundesliga on Saturday. item.title: Aces Misiorowski, Rasmussen to take mound for Game 5 of World Series
item.description: Both teams are turning to their No. 1 pitcher in Game 5 of the World Series at Tropicana Field on Oct. 28, with Jacob Misiorowski and Drew Rasmussen heading to the hill for their respective teams. On paper, that matchup favors the Milwaukee Brewers, and not just because Misiorowski is the presumed favorite to win the National League Cy Young. Rasmussen is pitching on just three days rest, and his last start didn't go great, when the Brewers got to him for three earned runs on six hits in 3⅔ innings in Game 2 of the series. Rasmussen, the former Brewers hurler who was traded to the Rays in 2021, hasn't pitched on short rest in his career since becoming a regular starter. Misiorowski will pitching on a normal four days rest, but it's not typical for him to work with less than five days between starts. He's only worked on four days rest in four starts this year, most recently on Sept. 20, but the other three occasions were all before the all-star break. For what it's worth, he's been good in those four outings, allowing four earned runs in 22 innings. But that Sept. 20 outing against Baltimore was only a three-inning performance as the team ramped down his workload heading for the postseason. Misiorowski comes into the game having thrown an even 188 innings this year between the regular season and playoffs. That's a marked jump from his 141⅓ innings last year, combining minors, MLB and playoffs. The Brewers haven't pushed him deep into playoff games, with 13⅓ innings over three starts. He's allowed four earned runs on 13 hits with five walks and 14 strikeouts (2.70 ERA). Rasmussen is also well past his career-high in innings, with 196⅔ innings this year. He threw 150 last year. His 2.67 ERA over 30 starts made him one of the best pitchers in the American League this year, and he still has a 2.19 ERA this postseason (six earned runs in 24⅔ innings) despite the rockier outing against Milwaukee. He carried a no-hitter into the eighth against the Yankees on Oct. 3 in the ALDS. item.description: Credit: Fox 13 Tampa Bay The Tampa Bay Rays avoided a World Series sweep Tuesday night, and Taylor Walls took offense when Ken Rosenthal suggested that the Rays should be happy they at least salvaged one moral victory. With a ring of reporters looking on, the shortstop bristled at the premise that the American League champions had to win a game to prove they deserved to share a field with the Brewers. “I think that’s pretty disrespectful, honestly,” he answered. “We’re a team that’s capable of winning four… No team wants to get swept, but at the end of the day, we think we can win the whole thing.” WATCH: “At the end of the day, we think we can win the whole thing.” #Rays shortstop Taylor Walls says it is disrespectful to think this team could just win one WS game. item.title: Every Time NASCAR Stripped A Win For Yellow Line Violations
item.description: Sam Sharpe-USA TODAY Sports NASCAR has stripped the victory from a driver four times in history because they crossed the yellow line. This rule was made to keep fans and drivers safe at superspeedways. Three of these losses happened in points-paying races across the three national divisions. The fourth loss occurred in an exhibition race. The rule is about 25 years old, but it still causes loud arguments after every big race. The debate flared up again on October 25, 2026, when Kyle Larson won the YellaWood 500 at Talladega. Larson beat William Byron by just 0.041 seconds after a late charge. Officials reviewed the finish and found Larson’s tires stayed on the line. He kept the win, but drivers like Denny Hamlin and Ryan Blaney are still asking for clearer rules. They want to know exactly how much of a tire can hang over the line before it counts as a foul. The Infamous 2008 Talladega Call The most famous penalty happened in the fall of 2008 at Talladega. Tony Stewart led a long line of cars on the final lap. Regan Smith tried to pass Stewart on the inside in the tri-oval. Stewart pushed hard and crowded Smith, forcing him to go completely below the yellow line. Smith crossed the finish line first, but NASCAR took the win away and gave it to Stewart. Smith argued that he had no choice but to go low to avoid a crash. He felt the rule should protect the driver who was forced down. “I always got told that the rule is if you get forced down there, you’re the winner of the race,” said Smith afterwards, according to Motorsport.com . He believed he had a nose inside and could have caused a big pile-up if he stayed up. “I had a nose inside of him, I could have piled up the whole field, and that would have been a cooler finish, I don’t know.” This bad call had a scary side effect the very next year. Brad Keselowski found himself in the same spot at Talladega in 2009. He did not yield to Carl Edwards. Edwards went airborne and flew into the catch-fencing. The safety risks of this rule are real, which is why it exists in the first place. Justin Haley’s Rookie Heartbreak Justin Haley lost his first Xfinity win in 2018 as a rookie making only his second start in the series. During the final lap, the lead was contested side-by-side by Elliott Sadler and Kyle Larson. Haley made a huge run and sliced underneath both of them. He flirted with the yellow line, and most fans thought he stayed on it. He crossed the finish line first and celebrated. However, NASCAR called it a violation and stripped the win. Larson inherited the victory. The Week 7 NFL slate included plenty of surprises for fantasy football managers, especially at the running back position. Superstar players like Jahmyr Gibbs and Bijan Robinson did not finish in the top 10 in terms of fantasy points. Instead, surprising players like Braelon Allen and Rhamondre Stevenson outperformed some of the best backs in the league. Those surprising outcomes can be a big part of the joy of playing fantasy football. But they can feel devastating when they result in your team losing a matchup. Fortunately, our Week 8 running back rankings are already here. And even better, this piece goes further in depth on a handful of players ahead of this weekend’s action. Week 8 Start ‘Em Running Backs Brett Davis-Imagn Images Ollie Gordon II, Dolphins vs. Patriots Gordon deserve some love after being unquestionably the best waiver wire player of the season. The Dolphins running back took over the backfield after De’Von Achane suffered a season-ending ACL injury . He is making the most of that opportunity approaching the midpoint of the 2026 season. Miami is clearly comfortable with Gordon as their lead back. That doesn’t always translate into success in fantasy football, but it seems to be working this time. Gordon has scored a touchdown in every game over the past four weeks. In those contests, he’s also gone over 100 rushing yards twice and been given 15+ carries on three occasions. His floor of ~14 fantasy points per game is quite good for a player who isn’t the best back on any fantasy manager’s roster. The Patriots do have a strong run defense unit. However, they’ve allowed rushing touchdowns at a pretty average clip this season. Gordon won’t win your Week 8 matchup all by himself. But he needs to be in every single lineup this week. He is an efficient runner (4.8 yards per carry) who also gets involved in the passing game (15 receptions for 115 yards, two touchdowns). Hubbard is also clearly the lead back in Carolina and has the production to prove it. He had scored 14+ fantasy points in every game this season before Week 7 against the Buccaneers. That time, the game script got away from him very early. As for this week’s matchup, Green Bay looks like an easy defense to run on. They’ve allowed 115 rushing yards per game this year alongside nine rushing touchdowns. That is more touchdowns than almost any other team in the league. Those figures would be even worse if Jahmyr Gibbs didn’t sit on what would’ve been an easy touchdown late in Week 7.
